column1: # walk of os/sys/h and os/sys/z8001/h against the resolved toolchain.

column3: REASON

column1: #   DIR      "sys/h" or "sys/z8001/h", relative to $OS -- which of the two
#            extra directories the row is about.
#   REASON   why the two texts are allowed to differ.  Free text, one line,
# A (DIR, BASENAME) pair that also exists in the toolchain ($TCINC or
# $TCINC/sys) and is NOT listed here must be byte-identical to the toolchain's
# copy, or the gate fails naming the file.  A pair that IS listed here but is
# no longer different from the toolchain's copy is also reported (a stale row
# hides a divergence that stopped existing, which is its own kind of rot).
# Background: os/sys/h and os/sys/z8001/h are 0.7.3-donor snapshots.  Under
# the kernel's own build (link-kernel.sh's IMI, which kheaders.py's IPATH
# mirrors), os/sys/h is not on the include path at all, and os/sys/z8001/h
# sits AFTER $TCINC and $TCINC/sys, so any basename the toolchain also
# carries is read from the toolchain, not from either of these directories.
# The one config that reads os/sys/z8001/h ahead of the toolchain is
# link-kernel.sh's IMD, used only to compile sys/z8001/src/ddt.c (the
# <seg.h>, so of everything in os/sys/z8001/h, only proc.h and seg.h are ever
# actually read out of that directory by a real build -- see their rows below.

The Z8001 machine layer's own shape: fixed NUSEG 8 with SISSLIB/SIPSLIB shared-library slots. Textually different from the toolchain's sys/proc.h, which reaches the same NUSEG 8 / SISSLIB / SIPSLIB values through #ifdef Z8001 so one header serves every port; values agree for this target. Under IMI (the kernel proper) the toolchain copy wins, so this copy is inert there; under IMD (KDDT=1, ddt.c only) this directory precedes the toolchain and ddt.c reads THIS copy -- do not delete it as dead weight.

The Z8001 machine layer's own shape, paired with proc.h above. Textually different from the toolchain's sys/seg.h for the same portability-vs-single-target reason. Under IMI the toolchain copy wins; under IMD (ddt.c) this copy is what gets read -- do not delete it as dead weight.
